newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mills reject 15,000 tns U.S. soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Manila mills reject 15,000 tns U.S. soybeans.

text.p: Philippine mills rejected on Wednesday offers for 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans due to high prices, traders said.
"We rejected all bids due to high prices," an executive in one of the mills told Reuters.
Philippine commodity traders said the firms sought tenders early on Wednesday for the supply of the soybeans for April shipment.
Philippine soybean and soymeal buyers said they may either shift buying to other countries or buy substitutes if U.S. prices remain at current high levels.
"We can buy corn if prices are better since soymeal is used as animal feed," said an industry executive.
Philippine soymeal imports this year for animal feed is expected to increase to 1.4 million tonnes from last year's 1.2 million, traders said.
Philippine companies also buy an average of 20,000 tonnes of soybeans monthly, traders said.
Last year, the Philippines bought 55 percent of its soybean and soymeal requirement from the United States, 30 percent from Brazil and the rest from India, Argentina and China, traders said.
Early today, traders said they expect Philippine soymeal and soybean buyers to shift to imports from other suppliers like South America due to high prices in the United States.
